reading: Twenty-two vendor-facing seams live in 15 modules or directories under src/lib, 2 under src/features and the Sentry wiring in src/instrumentation*.ts + src/app/observability.ts, all governed by one paragraph at docs/architecture/overview.md:107-111 that promises every vendor is "selected by env var and zod-validated at the boundary". That promise holds unevenly: 13 seams parse their config with zod, 7 hand-trim it (src/lib/address-lookup.ts:334, src/lib/observability/cloudwatch-config.ts:51 with a written 375 KB-bundle reason at lines 30-35, src/lib/notifications/web-push.ts:44, the three OAuth integrations, src/features/backup-export/platform-backup.ts:108), and 3 (Open-Meteo, the two NOAA modules) have no config at all. Degradation has three grammars: 8 `disabled*Provider` constants answering `{status:"not_configured"}` (45 non-test files return that status), 7 config readers answering `null`, and src/lib/rate-limit.ts:205 swapping in a real in-memory store. The same four lines are re-spelled per seam — 11 private `*Environment = Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>` aliases (five identical `PaymentEnvironment` in five Stripe files), 13 `type Fetch = typeof fetch` aliases, fetch injection spelled three ways (17 `fetchImpl: typeof fetch`, 12 `fetchImpl: Fetch`, 3 `fetcher: Fetcher`), and 20 `*FromEnvironment`/config functions. The e2e fleet's "never calls a vendor" promise is a union rather than a mechanism: `DIVEDAY_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_HTTP` is checked in 8 files in three grammars (flag alone → null; flag && real fetch → null; flag → fixture), 20 credential keys are blanked by hand at playwright.config.ts:110-129, and the comment at line 105 still says the flag "only covers the three integrations that read it directly". config/env-registry.mjs opens by claiming to hold "Every environment variable DiveDay reads" and holds 62 keys in 21 groups, while src/ reads 99 distinct keys — 41 unregistered, among them VAPID ×3 (web-push.ts:50-52, called "environment secrets" by ADR 20260804-manifest-web-push), UPSTASH ×2 (rate-limit.ts:202) and 10 per-cron `SENTRY_*_CRON_MONITOR_SLUG` overrides — and nothing in scripts/check-env.mjs ties a read in src/ to a row. Five registries each key on a vendor-shaped thing with no shared id — config/env-registry.mjs (21 groups), src/lib/cost-guardrails.ts (6 ceilings, `CostProvider`), infra/lib/manual-actions.ts (`ManualAction`), infra/lib/observability.ts (27 signals), src/features/integrations/registry.ts (4 providers) — plus two hand-written vendor tables at docs/README.md:41-55 and docs/architecture/aws-migration-dossier.md:45-51. Sentry is the one vendor whose SDK is imported outside a seam: 15 `@sentry/nextjs` import sites, 30 `Sentry.captureCheckIn(` calls, and 11 cron routes (1,592 lines) each carrying the same posture by hand — `CRON_SECRET` bearer gate (11), `maxDuration` (11), a monitor slug (10), a `checkinMargin` block (10), a completion log line (11) — while src/lib/cron-schedule.ts, whose test pins lockstep with vercel.json, is imported by exactly one of them. Runbook coverage is 13 files and 4,539 lines in docs/engineering, per-vendor for SES (580), SMS receipts (104), WhatsApp (120), CloudWatch (245), Sentry (97), rate limiting (300) and cost (241), and absent for Stripe, AWS Location, Open-Meteo, NOAA, web push and the four integrations (which have src/features/integrations/README.md instead).

ideas.title: Twenty-two seams, five registries, and no vendor id
ideas.reading: docs/architecture/overview.md:107-111 is the only place the seam concept is stated, and it states it as prose: measured against the code, 13 of 22 seams zod-validate, 7 hand-trim and 3 have no config. Five registries already key on a vendor-shaped thing with no shared id — config/env-registry.mjs (21 groups), src/lib/cost-guardrails.ts (`CostProvider`, 6 ceilings), infra/lib/manual-actions.ts, infra/lib/observability.ts (27 signals), src/features/integrations/registry.ts (4 providers) — and docs/README.md:41-55 and docs/architecture/aws-migration-dossier.md:45-51 hand-list vendors a sixth and seventh time. config/env-registry.mjs:1-2 claims to hold every variable DiveDay reads, and src/ reads 41 keys it does not hold, including VAPID ×3, UPSTASH ×2 and 10 SENTRY_*_CRON_MONITOR_SLUG overrides; scripts/check-env.mjs checks .env.example against the registry and .env.manual's provenance but never a read in src/. playwright.config.ts:110-129 blanks 20 credential keys by hand because nothing says which seams degrade on credentials and which on the flag. docs/engineering/cost-guardrails-runbook.md:181 says it outright: "a new vendor is invisible". Seven vendors have a runbook and eight do not, and no row anywhere says which.
ideas.idea: One seam registry, config/seams.mjs (plain .mjs for the same three-consumer reason env-registry gives at lines 16-20), with one row per seam: id, purpose, module path, provider and fake names, env group, degrade mode (`credentials` | `flag` | `fixture`), runbook path or `none:` with a reason, ADR ids, cost-ceiling ids, manual-action ids. env-registry's groups gain `seam:` (the four compiled-in overrides get an `override` provenance instead of being unlisted), `CostProvider` and manual-actions' vendor references become seam ids, and docs/README.md's runbook rows and the dossier's vendor table are rendered from the registry the way manual-actions.md already is. A `check:seams` guard holds three lines: every `env.X`/`process.env.X` read under src/ names a registered key or a listed exemption; every vendor SDK import and external host literal under src/ sits inside a registered seam's module; every seam row names a runbook or a reason. playwright.config.ts derives its blank list from every seam whose degrade mode is `credentials`, and `pnpm agent:health` gains a seam-coverage table (interface / fake / config parse / degrade mode / runbook / ceiling per seam) beside its "guards with no test" table. The grammar afterwards: a vendor is a row, and everything that mentions a vendor — env, cost, manual steps, runbook index, the e2e blank list — derives from it.
ideas.dissolves: The overview's prose promise and env-registry's false "every variable" claim; the two hand-written vendor tables; the 20 hand-blanked keys; the possibility of a vendor with no runbook, no ceiling and no env row going unnoticed.
ideas.scope: New config/seams.mjs (+ .d.mts); config/env-registry.mjs; scripts/check-seams.mjs + test and a check:repo row; scripts/check-env.mjs; scripts/agent-health.mjs; src/lib/cost-guardrails.ts (CostProvider); infra/lib/manual-actions.ts; playwright.config.ts:60-129; docs/README.md, docs/architecture/overview.md:107, docs/agents/repo-checks.md, docs/architecture/aws-migration-dossier.md:45-51; .claude/rules/infra.md and domain.md pointers; one ADR.
ideas.firstSlice: Land config/seams.mjs with 22 rows and `check:seams` in report-only mode naming the 41 unregistered keys and the 15 out-of-seam SDK imports; add `seam:` to every env-registry group and render docs/README.md's runbook rows from it.
ideas.conflicts: ADR 20260812-env-provenance-registry (extended one level up — its "a value the repo knows does not belong" rule is kept as an `override` provenance rather than silence); ADR 20260806-provider-usage-guardrails (CostProvider becomes derived, ceilings unchanged); ADR 20260805-cdk-minted-credentials-and-manual-actions (rows gain a seam id); H-45 and the aws-migration-dossier (its AWS-n rows stay, its vendor table becomes a view); #1826 (a send queue that gives up tells nobody — the per-seam "who watches" column is where that answer lives); #1721 (erasure for non-payment providers — a per-seam holds-personal-data column subsumes the question); #1661 (S3 cost attribution — seam rows name their buckets).

ideas.title: Every seam re-spells four lines; one seam kit replaces them
ideas.reading: Twenty selection points (18 exported `*FromEnvironment` plus readCloudWatchLogsConfig and webPushConfig) each re-declare their inputs: 11 private `*Environment` aliases of one Readonly<Record> type, five of them the identical `PaymentEnvironment` in src/lib/payments/{checkout,connect,customers,invoicing,promotions}.ts, and 13 `type Fetch = typeof fetch` aliases with injection spelled three ways (17/12/3). Those five Stripe files also each parse `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` through five one-key `configSchema`s (checkout.ts:149, customers.ts:51, invoicing.ts:150, promotions.ts:94, connect.ts:69) and each keep a `disabled*Provider`. Degradation is three grammars — 8 disabled providers answering not_configured, 7 readers answering null, rate-limit.ts:205 substituting a real store — so a caller learns each seam's answer by reading it. The kill switch is checked in 8 files in three grammars (cloudwatch-config.ts:54 and web-push.ts:49 ignore injection; marine-forecast.ts:335, usage/probe.ts:70, analytics.ts:264 and ingest-url.ts:144 gate on the real fetch; tide-predictions.ts:155-163 and tide-stations.ts:172 serve a fixture behind a DIVEDAY_E2E belt), and every SDK-backed seam ignores it, which is why playwright.config.ts blanks 20 keys and its line-105 comment counts three readers where there are eight. src/lib/usage/probe.ts:24-71 already names the shape — ProbeOptions, externalHttpBlocked, four sample states — for two seams only.
ideas.idea: One module, src/lib/seam.ts, holds the four lines every seam needs: `Environment`, `Fetch`, `externalHttpBlocked(env, fetcher)` promoted out of usage/probe.ts, and `seam({ env, read, build, disabled, blocked? })` — one selection function shape that trims flat string config (generalising cloudwatch-config.ts's no-zod reason; zod stays for payload parsing, which is what most of the 22 zod importers already are), returns `disabled` when a key is missing, and returns `blocked ?? disabled` under the flag whatever the credentials say. Every `*FromEnvironment` becomes a `seam()` call; Stripe's five become one `stripeConfigFromEnvironment` feeding five builders; the two tide modules pass their fixture as `blocked`, keeping ADR 20260907's rule as a parameter instead of a belt. Because the flag now beats credentials inside the kit, playwright.config.ts stops blanking keys and one test in seam.test.ts proves the fleet's no-vendor promise for every seam at once; `check:seams` (L25-1) refuses a new selection function outside the kit. The grammar afterwards is one sentence: a seam reads its env through `seam()`, degrades to `disabled`, and is blocked by the flag.
ideas.dissolves: 11 env aliases, 13 fetch aliases, three injection spellings, 8 disabled constants plus 7 null-returning readers, three kill-switch grammars, and the 20-key blank list — one grammar in one file.
ideas.scope: src/lib/seam.ts (new) and its test; the 20 selection points across src/lib/notifications (index, sms, whatsapp-signup, inbound-mail-store, web-push), src/lib/payments ×5, src/lib/storage (index, blob-host), src/lib/address-lookup.ts, src/lib/rate-limit.ts, src/lib/observability/cloudwatch-config.ts, src/lib/usage (probe, neon, vercel), src/lib/marine-forecast.ts, src/lib/tide-predictions.ts, src/lib/tide-stations.ts, src/lib/analytics.ts, src/lib/storage/ingest-url.ts, src/features/integrations ×3, src/features/backup-export/platform-backup.ts; their 54 test files; playwright.config.ts:60-129 and e2e/servers.ts:119-127; docs/architecture/overview.md:107; ADR 20260907-noaa-tide-predictions cross-reference; one ADR.
ideas.firstSlice: Create src/lib/seam.ts with Environment, Fetch, externalHttpBlocked and seam(); migrate usage/probe.ts, marine-forecast.ts and the two tide modules (the seams that already read the flag), deleting their local aliases and checks.
ideas.conflicts: ADR 20260907-noaa-tide-predictions (fixture-on-block survives as the `blocked` parameter; "right or absent" is kept); ADR 20260806-provider-usage-guardrails (probe.ts's shape is promoted, not changed); ADR 20260719-msw-offline-sync-only (unchanged — injection stays the unit-test seam, MSW stays at the offline boundary); src/lib/observability/cloudwatch-config.ts:30-35's no-zod reason (honoured and generalised); #1826 (the kit's not_configured/unavailable split is what lets a queue say which one it hit).

ideas.title: Sentry is the vendor without a seam; the cron routes are its door
ideas.reading: Every vendor SDK in src/ is imported inside its seam except one: `@sentry/nextjs` is imported at 15 sites — 11 cron routes, src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts, src/app/observability.ts and the two instrumentation files — with 30 captureCheckIn, 17 captureException and 7 captureMessage calls spread across src/. The 11 cron routes total 1,592 lines and each restates one posture by hand: a CRON_SECRET bearer gate (11 files), maxDuration (11), a per-route monitor slug read from an unregistered SENTRY_*_CRON_MONITOR_SLUG key (10), a checkinMargin block (10) and a completion log line (11); src/app/api/cron/usage/route.ts:82-86 says it "fails closed exactly like /api/cron/retention and /api/cron/reminders", which is the copy admitting it is a copy. src/lib/cron-schedule.ts exists to pin one schedule to vercel.json by test and is imported by exactly one of the eleven, so ten schedules are asserted nowhere. The dossier names "AWS-3a Sentry decoupling" as a sequencing item (docs/architecture/aws-migration-dossier.md, H-45) and docs/engineering/monitoring-runbook.md is 97 lines, the shortest vendor runbook. src/lib/observability/cloudwatch.ts:48-56 already shows how a framework-bound hook enters src/lib: injected, never imported.
ideas.idea: Two things become one shape. First, an error-and-check-in seam in src/lib/observability (a `Reporter` interface: captureException, captureMessage, checkIn; a disabled reporter; a sink registered once from src/instrumentation.ts the way FlushDeferrer is), so the 24 capture sites import `@/lib/observability` and the SDK is imported in three files. Second, `cronRoute({ id, schedule, maxDuration, run })` in src/lib — the bearer gate, the check-in pair around `run`, the `diveday-<id>` slug with one `SENTRY_<ID>_CRON_MONITOR_SLUG` override read in one place, the `cron_<id>.scan_complete` line, and the vercel.json lockstep assertion extended from one schedule to eleven through cron-schedule.test.ts. Each route becomes its `run` body; the ten slug keys become one registered pattern row in the seam registry (L25-1). The grammar afterwards: a cron is a name, a schedule and a body, and Sentry is a seam like SES.
ideas.dissolves: The hand-copied posture in 11 routes, 12 of 15 SDK import sites, ten unregistered env keys, and the unasserted lockstep of ten schedules.
ideas.scope: src/lib/observability/ (new reporter + cron-route modules and tests), src/instrumentation.ts, src/app/observability.ts, the 11 src/app/api/cron/*/route.ts files and their tests, src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts, src/lib/cron-schedule.ts + test, vercel.json (read by the test), config/env-registry.mjs (slug pattern row), docs/engineering/monitoring-runbook.md, .claude/rules/infra.md, one ADR.
ideas.firstSlice: Add `cronRoute()` with a test asserting 503-unconfigured, 401-wrong-token and the check-in pair, and adopt it in the three smallest routes (integrations 29 lines, recaps 51, trip-reminders 78) — no reporter seam yet.
ideas.conflicts: ADR 20260806-provider-usage-guardrails ("copying /api/cron/retention's posture exactly" becomes one call; posture unchanged); ADR 20260727-sentry-error-monitoring-q7fk2p (kept — the seam is where its redaction and DSN already live); dossier AWS-3a / H-45 (this is the code half of the decoupling, not a migration); ADR 20260806-cloudwatch-log-shipping's FlushDeferrer precedent (reused for the reporter sink); .claude/rules/domain.md's framework-free src/lib (honoured by injection).
